answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding each identity to an escrow: when k coordinated identities equivocate on the same event, correlated penalties grow as O(k²), rather than being assessed as unrelated single-node faults. Detection applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, so operating a larger swarm compounds exposure; asymmetric depreciation makes seized collateral harder to replace. This ripple effect anchors accountability across the network, even in a sparse tundra of otherwise independent nodes.
